about: Rules for planning an A/B split in a Bloomreach Engagement scenario and sizing the test. scripts/ab_split_plan.py and scripts/ab_test_duration.py read this file (their defaults come from it), so change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes.

notes.writable_statuses: Scenario statuses the split may be added to in place with update_scenario. Nothing runs in them, so the change has no live impact.
notes.copy_statuses: Running statuses. The skill never edits these in place (it never passes allow_active); with a copy_name in the test spec it plans a new draft copy with create_scenario instead, otherwise the change is blocked.
notes.managed_fields: Top-level scenario fields the backend manages, removed from the payload before a write (the same list engagement-scenario-builder uses). A top-level customer_filter is also refused by the write tools.
notes.message_node_types: Node types that send a message and carry their content in a design. A message test needs one of these after the split.
notes.no_design_node_types: Node types that carry no design (triggers, waits, conditions, splits, limits, labels, set-property, add-event and webhooks; type names from engagement-scenario-builder's references/node-config.md). Every other node type is treated as carrying content in a design, including serve-banner-action, in-app message steps and any type not listed here: one of them without a design means the scenario was fetched without include_node_designs=true, so the plan is blocked, because a full update would wipe the content. verify also checks that every node that had a design in the payload still has one in the read-back.
notes.timing_node_types: Node types a timing test can vary: the wait right after the split point. Only wait-action's fields (units, count) were seen on real scenarios; other waits aren't verified.
notes.split_node_types: Split node types. Only ab-split is built (its shape was seen on real scenarios); the others are counted when warning that the scenario already has a split.
notes.min_variant_percentage: Smallest share of traffic either branch may get. Below it, the smaller branch takes too long to reach a readable sample.
notes.max_holdout_percentage: Largest share a holdout (the branch that sends nothing) may get. A bigger holdout withholds the message from most customers: a warning.
notes.relative_lifts: Relative lifts the duration estimate sizes for when the user gives none (0.1 = +10%).
notes.z_alpha: z value for a two-sided 5% significance level, as in discovery-experiment-setup's estimate_duration.py.
notes.min_test_days: Shortest recommended test, in days. Tests run in whole weeks so weekday and weekend customers are both covered. engagement-experiment-readout uses the same minimum.
notes.max_test_weeks: If even the largest lift needs longer than this, the estimate says the test isn't practical as set up (too few customers reach that step).
